drivingQuestion: Why is a dead gentile pure?
outcomeNote: a baraita supplies the reason for the mishna's ruling

segments.he: נׇכְרִי שֶׁמֵּת [כּוּ׳]. תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ נׇכְרִי שֶׁמֵּת טָהוֹר מִלְּטַמֵּא בְּמַשָּׂא? לְפִי שֶׁאֵין טוּמְאָתוֹ מֵחַיִּים מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, אֶלָּא מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: With regard to the corpse of «a gentile who died,» although when alive he transmits impurity like a zav, once he dies he is ritually pure and is prevented from transmitting impurity. «It is taught» in a baraita that «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «said: For what» reason «did» the Sages «say» that the corpse of «a gentile who died is ritually pure» and is prevented «from transmitting impurity by carrying? Because his impurity» that he transmits even «when alive is not by Torah law, but by rabbinic law.» The Sages decreed that every living gentile imparts ritual impurity in the manner of a zav; they did not extend their decree to include the corpse of a gentile in the manner of the corpse of a zav.
